name: NX996 · Notification Outbox Sender (Gmail, vendor pipeline)

nodes.name: Every 5 Minutes
nodes.notes: NX996 outbox sender. Drains public.nexus_notification_outbox (the NEXUS vendor sales-enquiry pipeline -- deliberately NOT tenant-scoped; see the migration's own verified guard against a tenant_id column ever being added to this table). Every 5 minutes is a compromise between the queue's own 60s-1h exponential backoff floor and not hammering Gmail; adjust freely, nothing here assumes this exact interval.

nodes.name: Claim Due Notifications
nodes.notes: nexus_notification_claim is a lease, not a state change (NX996 doc comment): a retry after a dropped response either claims nothing new (nothing was due yet) or claims a fresh batch -- it can never re-claim the same row twice, so retryOnFail is safe here the way it is not on the mark_sent/mark_failed state-transition calls below. p_channel:'EMAIL' because this sender only speaks Gmail; WHATSAPP/SLACK rows (none exist today) are left PENDING for a future worker rather than silently drained here.

nodes.name: Normalize Claimed Rows
nodes.notes: One n8n item per claimed notification. 0 claimed -> 0 items -> execution stops here, which IS success (nothing was due), not a failure.

nodes.name: Fetch Sales Lead
nodes.notes: GET, not an RPC: nexus_sales_lead has no dedicated read accessor (NX996 built this sender for a server-side key, same boundary as nexus_notification_status -- see that function's own comment). The Supabase credential here runs as service_role, which bypasses RLS entirely, exactly like every other supabaseApi-credentialed node in this repo. onError:'continueRegularOutput' turns a fetch failure into data ({error: ...}) instead of aborting the whole batch -- Build Email Content classifies it next, mirroring Delivery Report's pattern in ops/site-enquiry/site-enquiry.workflow.json.

nodes.name: Build Email Content
nodes.notes: The only place that decides whether this notification can actually be emailed. A false here never throws -- it flows to Mark Failed below with a real error_code, so a bad row gets recorded as FAILED/RETRYING instead of quietly stalling for a full 300s lease.

nodes.name: Sendable?
nodes.notes: TRUE -> send. FALSE -> Mark Failed (Lookup) directly; there is nothing to send.

nodes.name: Send via Gmail
nodes.notes: Node type, typeVersion and the gmailOAuth2 credential id (1Cgivoyjt7psAirH) copied verbatim from ops/site-enquiry/site-enquiry.workflow.json's 'Email: Site Enquiry (Gmail)' node so this binds to the credential that already exists, rather than inventing a second Gmail connection for the same vendor pipeline. onError is 'continueRegularOutput' ONLY so a failed send reaches Delivery Report below instead of vanishing -- do not remove Delivery Report and leave this onError in place.

nodes.name: Mark Sent

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_notification_id: $json.notification_id, p_worker: 'n8n-notification-outbox-sender', p_detail: 'gmail message id ' + ($json.messageId || '(unknown)') }) }}

nodes.notes: State transition, not idempotent (nexus_notification_mark_sent refuses SENT->SENT -- NX996's own transition table has no such row) -- deliberately no retryOnFail here, unlike Claim above. onError:'continueRegularOutput' so one item's mark failure cannot abort the rest of the batch; a swallowed failure here still surfaces because the row stays SENT-but-unwritten only in the sender's own eyes -- nexus_notification_status() will keep reporting the true DB state on the next read regardless.

nodes.name: Mark Failed (Lookup)
nodes.notes: Reached when Build Email Content decided this claimed row cannot be emailed at all (lead fetch failed, lead missing, or lead has no email). Records the real reason so a human reading nexus_notification_status()/last_error_detail is not left guessing.
